question: What will be the percentage change in front-month WTI crude oil futures (CL=F on Yahoo Finance) from the close on 2026-08-18 to the close on 2026-09-02?
resolution_criteria: Resolves to 100 x (close on 2026-09-02 / close on 2026-08-18 - 1), using daily closes of CL=F on Yahoo Finance. If there is no close on 2026-09-02, the last close before it is used.
baseline:
Computed by code from Yahoo Finance daily closes for CL=F: latest close 84.9400 on 2026-08-18.
Target date 2026-09-02 is 10 trading observations ahead. Percentiles of the price on the target date,
from the empirical distribution of 10-observation returns over the last 3 years (last year weighted double):
p5: 74.4688, p10: 78.0193, p25: 81.7872, p50: 85.1025, p75: 88.2074, p90: 92.0546, p95: 99.2199
This ignores news and known events; adjust for them. Check the symbol matches the resolution source
(exchange, contract month, close vs settlement price).
research:
I found nothing that settles the outcome early. Front-month WTI was in the mid-$80s on Aug 18-19 and rising, driven by the US-Iran stalemate over the Strait of Hormuz. Direct page fetches failed through the proxy, so the figures below come from search-result snippets.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-08-18: Yahoo Finance CL=F closed at **84.94**, per the code-collected data. That close was the **September contract (CLU26)**.
- I could not open the Yahoo page directly.
- **Contract roll:** CLU26 should stop trading around 2026-08-20, which is three business days before Aug 25 under CME's rule. CL=F should then switch to **October (CLV26)**. If so, the Sep 2 close is October's price compared against September's base, so any gap between the two months gets built into the result.
- Undated: a Barchart snapshot showed CLV26 at 86.18, up 1.79. If that was Aug 19, October closed near 84.39 the day before, about $0.55 below September's 84.94. I could not confirm the date. [Barchart via search](https://www.barchart.com/futures/quotes/WIU26)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has happened that settles or nearly settles the question.
- 2026-08-19: Barchart commentary said September WTI closed up 0.89 (+1.05%), roughly 85.8, at a 4-week high. [Barchart](https://www.barchart.com/futures/quotes/CLQ26)
- 2026-08-19: CNBC headline: "Oil prices rise more than 1% as Middle East crisis escalates." [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/19/oil-edges-up-on-uncertainty-over-exports-through-hormuz.html)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-18: WTI was up 1.4% at $85.68 and Brent at $91.78 during the session. Iran said it would take a more offensive stance and keep Hormuz shut until the US meets the June interim deal's terms. Trump said no talks were happening but that the strait was open. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/18/oil-climbs-as-fading-us-iran-peace-hopes-raise-supply-risks.html)
- 2026-08-17/18: Bloomberg said oil was at a 3-week high as the US signalled no rush to end the conflict. [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-08-17/latest-oil-market-news-and-analysis-for-aug-18)
- 2026-08-17: The 60-day US-Iran memorandum signed June 17 expired without an extension. Brent rose above $90 ($91.36). Trump threatened Oman. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/17/oil-prices-iran-war-strait-hormuz.html), [AGBI](https://www.agbi.com/oil-and-gas/2026/08/oil-rises-above-90-as-us-iran-interim-deal-expires/), [CNN](https://www.cnn.com/2026/08/17/world/live-news/iran-war-trump), [The National](https://www.thenationalnews.com/news/us/2026/08/16/deadline-for-us-iran-agreement-expires-with-stalemate-set-to-continue/)
- 2026-08-13: Oil fell after the US said crude exports through Hormuz were near 9 million barrels per day. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/13/oil-spill-near-oman-worries-over-supply-.html)
- 2026-08-12: Attacks on shipping lifted Brent to about $90. The EIA does not expect Middle East output to get back near pre-war levels until early 2027. [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/8/12/oil-prices-rise-as-attacks-dent-hopes-for-strait-of-hormuz-reopening)
- 2026-08-11: US crude rose above $83 after Iran said the strait would not reopen until its conditions were met. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/11/oil-prices-today-us-crude-84.html)
- Week to 2026-08-07: Brent fell about 7% when Treasury Secretary Bessent hinted a Hormuz deal was near, then rose when Iran published restrictive draft conditions for the strait. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/06/oil-price-iran-war-strait-hormuz-oman-deal.html)
- Context: the wartime peak was above $110 (Brent, May). Brent rose 24% in July.
- **Takeaway:** prices swing sharply on deal and no-deal headlines, by about 7% in a week in both directions this month.

## 4. Base rates
- From the code-computed 10-trading-day return distribution over 3 years, with the last year weighted double:
  - p5: 74.47 (-12.3%)
  - p10: 78.02 (-8.1%)
  - p25: 81.79 (-3.7%)
  - p50: 85.10 (+0.2%)
  - p75: 88.21 (+3.8%)
  - p90: 92.05 (+8.4%)
  - p95: 99.22 (+16.8%)
- The tails are wide and skewed upward, reflecting war-driven volatility.
- The September-to-October switch adds a level shift. If October is about $0.5 below September, that is roughly -0.6%, but the spread is unconfirmed.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Mid-Aug 2026: Polymarket ran "What will WTI hit in August 2026" (touch markets, not closing prices). The $85 high was at about 61.5% Yes in a snapshot. $100 and $120 were near 0%. [Polymarket](https://polymarket.com/event/what-price-will-wti-hit-in-august-2026), [polyguana](https://polyguana.com/events/what-price-will-wti-hit-in-august-2026)
- 2026-08-18: Robinhood's daily WTI settle contracts priced "Above $83.99" at 96¢ and "Above $86.99" at 2¢. [Robinhood](https://robinhood.com/us/en/prediction-markets/financial/events/oil-price-wti-on-aug-18-2026-aug-18-2026/)
- I found no Kalshi or Polymarket market for WTI on Sep 2, and no bank forecasts for that horizon.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- About 2026-08-20: September contract expires and CL=F rolls to October.
- Ongoing: US-Iran standoff over Hormuz now that the interim deal has lapsed. Any talks, deal, escalation or shipping attack could move prices by several percent in a day.
- Weekly EIA petroleum status reports on about Aug 19, Aug 26 and Sep 2.
- Late August (dates unconfirmed): the Fed's Jackson Hole symposium.
- The next OPEC+ meeting is probably early September, possibly after Sep 2. I could not confirm the date.
- Labor Day (Sep 7) falls after the window, so a Sep 2 close is expected.
